audit.why: EVEN 6/10 is consistent with 52.37% over 506 games and a level chart that trades stages before tilting to Rumble at two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-3 and level-6 spikes describe the wrong mechanics: Tangle-Barbs is said to 'root through multiple targets — she can hit you, her clone, and a minion all at once', and Pop Blossom is called 'a massive AOE stun'.
audit.why: Riot's text says Tangle-Barbs grows LARGER, FASTER and roots LONGER after it passes through a champion or kills a unit — the danger is not multi-hit, it is that a minion in the way upgrades the root that reaches you. Pop Blossom is a knockup first and a stun on landing, on a 120-second cooldown at rank 1, and neither the two-part CC nor the cooldown was stated.
audit.corrected: Both spikes rewritten with the real mechanics and the real cooldowns.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json (E Tangle-Barbs cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10; R Pop Blossom cd 120/105/90)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three things. (a) 'Blooming Burst Q pokes at roughly the same range' as Flamespitter. (b) 'let the slow negate Pop Blossom's window'. (c) 'the clone has no shadow, runs forward, and fades quickly' offered as a reliable tell.
audit.why: (a) Blooming Burst is 800 range against Flamespitter's 600 — she out-ranges you by a third and the lane's whole shape follows from that. (b) Pop Blossom is a leap; a move-speed slow does not deny a leap, so the advice invites the player to stand in Equalizer and eat the ult anyway. (c) Shapesplitter's clone can be redirected mid-flight by recast, so 'runs forward' is not a tell, and the no-shadow claim is not in the kit data.
audit.corrected: Range gap stated, the slow claim replaced with spacing, the clone tell replaced with the recast-redirect fact.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json (Q Blooming Burst range 800; W Shapesplitter recast redirects the clone; R Pop Blossom: dash/leap)

audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs is the tracked cooldown on every panel but its length is never given; 'her root cooldown is long enough' is all the player gets.
audit.why: 12 seconds at rank 1 falling to 10 at rank 5 is a short window, not a generous one — the vague wording invites over-committing.
audit.corrected: 12s at rank 1 stated in the cooldown breakdown, the Do entry and the level-3 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour is never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's own text says Pop Blossom's preparation is HIDDEN while Neeko is disguised — a Neeko wearing your jungler's model can ult you with no wind-up. That is the single hidden mechanic that decides deaths in this matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Added to the level-6 spike and whys[4].
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json (P Inherent Glamour; R Pop Blossom: 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised')

edits.before: Level 1 is a standoff — your Flamespitter has reach but Neeko's Blooming Burst Q pokes at roughly the same range, and without Heat control feel yet you don't want to walk into a Tangle-Barbs. Farm passively and watch whether she leads with Q poke or tries to walk up; that tells you her intended pattern. At level 2 she has the edge because Tangle-Barbs coming online is a much bigger power spike than your E-slow addition — if she roots you she can follow with Blooming Burst and her passive colored-damage burst for a clean trade that you simply cannot win through. Respect the root completely at 2: the moment Tangle-Barbs is on cooldown is the ONLY safe window to step up. Level 3 is still hers: she can W to spawn a clone, bait your Harpoon onto it, then root the real you with E and burst. Identify where her clone is before committing anything — the clone has no shadow, runs forward, and fades quickly, but in the chaos of trading you will misread it.
edits.after: Level 1 is a standoff you lose on range — Blooming Burst reaches 800 to Flamespitter's 600, so she pokes for free and closing means walking into a 1000-range Tangle-Barbs. Farm passively and watch whether she leads with Q poke or tries to walk up; that tells you her intended pattern. Level 3 is still hers: she can W to spawn a clone, bait your Harpoon onto it, then root the real you with E and burst. Identify where her clone is before committing anything — she can recast Shapesplitter to redirect the clone mid-flight, so its heading is no tell — watch which body actually casts.

edits.before: Neeko's Tangle-Barbs (E) roots through multiple targets — she can hit you, her clone, and a minion all at once, giving her a free burst window while you're locked in place.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs (E) grows larger, faster and roots for longer after it passes through a champion or kills a unit — a minion in the way upgrades the root instead of blocking it. 12s at rank 1.

edits.before: Pop Blossom (R) is a massive AOE stun that punishes any moment you stand still or commit to a Flamespitter trade — she will W-clone to bait your engage then R you mid-channel.
edits.after: Pop Blossom (R) knocks up, then stuns on landing, and its wind-up is invisible while she wears an ally's face — 120s at rank 1, so one dodge buys you two minutes of free lane.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 genuinely split — her poke pattern with Q and clone baits is real, but her root cooldown is long enough that you can steal full Danger Zone trades in the gap. The rule is simple: track Tangle-Barbs exactly. When it's down, walk into her face and burn her with sustained Flamespitter; she has no escape in that window and your double-E slow ensures she takes the full channel. When the root is up, play at max Flamespitter range or back off entirely — a root mid-channel is a death sentence because you're silenced until Overheat clears. At level 6 she gets Pop Blossom, which is a stun, not just a root, and it punishes any stationary Flamespitter channel or post-Equalizer positioning. Use Equalizer defensively first — drop it between you and her when she goes for the all-in, and let the slow negate Pop Blossom's window. Your own Equalizer has way more range and map impact than hers, so start shaping river fights around it rather than chasing solo kills.
